title: Verbal sprint 2
description: Ten synonyms and ten sentence completions. The real ISEE gives about thirty seconds a question, and this set is timed the same way, so there is no prize for finishing early. For each completion, find the clue before reading the choices: although, but and rather than signal a contrast; because and so that signal a cause; a colon or a semicolon means the second half explains the first. Guessing is free on the ISEE, so answer every question.

questions.stem: METICULOUS
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail. Very careful is the match. Messy is the opposite. Mysterious and measurable are sound-alikes.

questions.stem: ADAMANT
questions.explanation: Adamant means refusing to change one's mind. Firmly determined is the match. Flexible is the opposite. Grown up is a trap from the sound of adult, and angry is an association: adamant people can sound heated, but being firm is not the same as being angry.

questions.stem: LUCID
questions.explanation: Lucid means clearly expressed and easy to understand. Clear is the match. Confusing is the opposite. Lucky and liquid are sound-alikes. A lucid explanation is one you understand the first time you hear it.

questions.stem: SKEPTICAL
questions.explanation: Skeptical means doubtful and not easily convinced. Doubtful is the match. Trusting is the opposite. Skeletal shares the first letters. A skeptical reader asks for evidence before believing a claim.

questions.stem: AMPLE
questions.explanation: Ample means enough, or more than enough. Plentiful is the match. Scarce is the opposite. Simple and sample are sound-alikes that differ by a letter or two.

questions.stem: RIGID
questions.explanation: Rigid means unable to bend. Stiff is the match. Bendable is the opposite. Frozen is a near miss, since frozen things are often rigid, but a steel bar is rigid at any temperature. Rapid is a sound-alike.

questions.stem: DEPLETE
questions.explanation: To deplete is to use up a supply until little or none is left. Use up is the match. Fill is the opposite. Delete and complete are sound-alikes; delete is close in feeling, but deleting removes something at once, while depleting wears a supply down.

questions.stem: COHERENT
questions.explanation: Coherent means logical and consistent, so that the parts fit together. Logical and clear is the match. Confused is the opposite. Sticky comes from cohere, which can mean stick together, and related is a guess from the same idea; in a test sentence, coherent describes an argument, a plan or a speaker.

questions.stem: SOLITARY
questions.explanation: Solitary means done or existing alone. Alone is the match. Crowded is the opposite. Sunny is a trap from sol, the root for sun, and solid shares the first letters.

questions.stem: VERIFY
questions.explanation: To verify is to check that something is true. Confirm is the match. Doubt is close to the opposite. Very is a sound-alike, and change comes from confusing verify with vary.

questions.stem: Although the first draft of her essay was __________, the final version was clear and well organised.
questions.explanation: Although signals a contrast with the second half, which calls the final version clear and well organised. So the first draft must have been the opposite: disorganised. Excellent agrees with the second half instead of contrasting with it, and lengthy says nothing about organisation. Find the signal word before reading the choices.

questions.stem: The committee's decision was __________: every single member voted in favour.
questions.explanation: The colon means the second half explains the first. Every member voting the same way is the definition of unanimous. Divided is the exact opposite. Delayed and secret are things a decision can be, but nothing after the colon supports them.

questions.stem: Because the instructions were so __________, nobody had any trouble assembling the shelf.
questions.explanation: Because means the blank causes the result, and the result is that nobody had trouble. Instructions that cause no trouble are straightforward. Brief is the trap: short instructions can still be confusing, and the sentence is about clarity, not length. Complicated is the opposite.

questions.stem: She argued with such __________ that even her opponents began to doubt their own position.
questions.explanation: Such blank that result means the blank caused the result. Opponents start doubting themselves when the speaker is deeply sure of her case, which is conviction. Volume is the trap: loud arguing rarely changes anyone's mind. Hesitation would have the opposite effect.

questions.stem: The forecast promised a calm afternoon, but within an hour the sea had turned __________.
questions.explanation: But signals a contrast with calm, so the sea became rough: turbulent. Tranquil means calm, which agrees with the forecast instead of contrasting with it. Shallow and warm describe a sea but do not contrast with calm.

questions.stem: The old bridge was declared __________ after engineers found deep cracks in its supports.
questions.explanation: The cracks are the reason for the declaration, so the blank must be what cracks make a bridge: unsafe. Historic and beautiful may be true of an old bridge, but nothing in the sentence supports them. The second half is the evidence, and the right word is the one the evidence proves.

questions.stem: Marcus is notoriously __________; he has been late to every practice this season.
questions.explanation: The semicolon means the second half explains the first, and being late to every practice is the definition of tardy. Punctual is the exact opposite. Tired might explain lateness, but the sentence describes the lateness itself, not a cause of it.

questions.stem: Rather than __________ the problem, the class decided to face it directly.
questions.explanation: Rather than sets up a contrast with facing the problem directly, so the blank is the opposite of facing it: evade, which means avoid. Solve is the trap, because it sounds like the right thing to do, but solving a problem is facing it, so it cannot be the thing the class chose not to do.

questions.stem: The museum's collection is so __________ that a visitor could spend a week there and still not see everything.
questions.explanation: So blank that result means the blank causes the result. Needing more than a week to see everything is caused by size, so the collection is vast. Valuable is the trap: an expensive collection can be small. Ancient and famous do not explain why it takes so long to see.

questions.stem: After months without rain, the reservoir was nearly __________.
questions.explanation: Months without rain use up the water in a reservoir, so it is nearly depleted, meaning used up. Overflowing is the opposite. Frozen and polluted are things that can happen to a reservoir, but neither follows from a lack of rain.
